title: Third Report and Order and Third FNPRM, Protecting Against National Security Threats to the Communications Supply Chain through the Equipment Authorization Program (FCC 26-50, ET Docket 21-232)
notes: Adopted 22 Jul, released 23 Jul 2026. 'the prohibitions … apply only for logic-bearing hardware components produced by an entity identified on the Covered List' (para. 37). Declines software/firmware 'given the lack of support in the record and the challenges with enforcement and oversight' (para. 30). Definition limited to components 'within our statutory authority to regulate under the Communications Act' (para. 31).

title: Protecting Against National Security Threats to the Communications Supply Chain Through the Equipment Authorization Program (final rule)
notes: Effective 30 days after publication (13 Oct 2026). Applies only to producer/provider-based Covered List entries, prospectively to new applications; pending applications exempt unless amended. 'The Commission declines, at this time, to adopt broader proposals.'

title: Chairman Carr Proposes to Strengthen Rules Governing Dangerous Gear (news release)
notes: Announcement of the proposal circulated to Commissioners, not the adopted rule. The phrase 'component part loophole' here is FCC staff background text, not Carr's quoted words; Carr's own wording is in PR-005.

title: Import Network Equipment into the US: FCC Covered List and IOR
notes: Commercial importer-of-record firm (discloses a commercial interest). 'Only producer-based entries trigger it … It does not reach the newer location-based entries … unless the component maker is separately listed.'

title: Statement of Chairman Brendan Carr on FCC 26-50
notes: 'First, we take action to finally and fully close the component part loophole.' … 'prohibit devices containing any Huawei-made logic-bearing hardware component (basically any “smart” component).'

title: Trump administration drafting ban on Chinese data center devices, sources say (Reuters exclusive, reprint)
notes: Four unnamed sources: ban on imports of new models; 'The FCC could still modify or shelve the restriction'; InnoLight 27% share (Counterpoint). Chinese Embassy: 'China will take all necessary measures in response to any action that causes material harm to its interests.' Quotes Divyansh Kaushik (Beacon Global Strategies): 'Transceivers definitely pose a risk.'

title: US FCC Weighs Chinese Transceiver Supply-Chain Crackdown
notes: 'No draft text has been released'; 'The FCC has not published a threat determination involving optical transceivers'. Open questions: definition of 'new model', whether 'Chinese' means nationality, Covered List inclusion or manufacturing location. Notes modules 'carry microcontrollers, nonvolatile memories and vendor firmware'. One internal dating error (October component action); not reused.

title: FCC Ban on New Chinese Optical Modules
notes: InnoLight 34% of $7.7B datacom optical component revenue (1Q26); Chinese-HQ ~60% of that metric. 3.2T enters production in 2028 (forecast). Argues 'revisions and cost reductions to 800G and 1.6T optics would certainly be considered new' and 'There is no bona fide security risk' (analyst opinion). Does NOT support a 3.2T phase-in.

title: FCC Chinese Optical Module Rules: What Changed Oct 13
notes: Vendor blog. Reports 3.2T phase-in 'according to reporting tied to Morgan Stanley meetings in Washington' (links only a Substack) and a 65% US BOM-value exemption (no outlet named); 'not yet codified'. Third-hand: used with care.

title: Innolight, Coherent, Lumentum: Who Wins and Loses in the Proposed FCC Ban on Chinese Transceivers?
notes: InnoLight ~27%, Coherent ~17%, Lumentum ~6% of module revenue; Chinese makers ~60% of revenue and nearly two-thirds of units. InnoLight and Eoptolink buy DSPs from Broadcom/Marvell and lasers from Lumentum, Coherent, Mitsubishi Electric; Thailand lines; Western competitors lack capacity 'within a 12-to-24-month horizon'.

title: Microsoft Reportedly Urges U.S. to Drop Proposed Chinese Optical Transceiver Ban Amid AI Supply Concerns
notes: Citing Reuters: Microsoft and others urged the administration to drop the plan (meetings with OSTP and NSC in September). Narrower ban on 3.2T 'according to Reuters, citing Morgan Stanley'. 65% BOM exemption 'according to Economic Daily News, citing Morgan Stanley' (the only source attributing it).

title: Chinese Optical Transceiver Ban: What Procurement Should Know
notes: Component broker. Citing Counterpoint: if the rule follows point of manufacture, Thai lines may fall outside it; if ownership, exposed anywhere. InnoLight + Eoptolink 'roughly 60% of NVIDIA's 800G volume' (attributed to Counterpoint, not in PR-014: second-hand). Rated 1.6T 'High' exposure (September, before 3.2T reporting).

title: Proposed U.S. ban on Chinese optical transceivers threatens AI data center boom
notes: Two unnamed networking vendors: confusion over finished modules vs components and subsidiaries; 'two to three years to stand up a rush job operation … five to 10 years' to reshore; 'it's not very easy to exfiltrate data via optical transceivers'. Misdescribes Reuters as 'all' transceivers (Reuters: new models).

title: FCC proposes import ban on Chinese optical transceivers
notes: Headline overstates: no FCC proposal has been published (PR-011). 56% = TrendForce's share of contract manufacturing capacity. Coherent and Lumentum 'already running at capacity and … around 30% overbought'. Contains a router-date error; used only for the capacity point.

title: Microsoft fighting Trump administration's proposed ban on Chinese optical transceivers: report
notes: Relays Reuters: Microsoft lobbying against the ban; officials looking at the highest data rates such as 3.2T, ramping around 2028. One factual error about Lumentum; not reused.

title: S.5548, Securing National Security Systems from Chinese Optical Transceivers Act of 2026
notes: URL not verified at build (HTTP 403). Text checked at PR-025 (GovInfo). Introduced 24 Sep 2026; referred to HSGAC.

title: Senate Bill Targets Chinese Transceivers in Federal Networks
notes: Covers InnoLight, Eoptolink, subsidiaries/affiliates and later-designated companies; five-year transition. Gives 'Sept. 25' as introduction date; GovInfo says 24 Sep.

title: Pentagon Adds 65 New Entities to the 1260H List of Chinese Military Companies
notes: Update of 8 Jun 2026 adds Zhongji Innolight as a parent-level listing. Entity contracting ban from 30 Jun 2026; product ban from 30 Jun 2027, which does not cover components inside end items.

title: Moolenaar: American Companies & Governments Should Cut Ties With New Pentagon-Listed Chinese Military Companies
publisher: House Select Committee on the CCP
notes: Committee chair statement; lists Zhongji Innolight among additions.

title: DoW releases list of Chinese military companies in accordance with Section 1260H
notes: The updated list identifies 188 entities.

title: S.5548 bill text (introduced in Senate, 24 Sep 2026)
notes: Covered optical transceivers designed, developed, manufactured or supplied by Zhongji Innolight, Eoptolink and subsidiaries/affiliates; prohibitions 'shall take effect five years after the date of the enactment'; FAR Council to update regulations within three years.

title: Senators McCormick, Gallego, Cornyn, Fetterman introduce bill to keep Chinese transceivers out of U.S. national security systems
notes: Sponsor quotes (bipartisan). Rationale: 'Because advanced transceivers can contain reprogrammable firmware, their use in national security networks can create potential supply-chain and security risks.'

title: China, the FCC, and the Logic of Transceivers
notes: Analysis/opinion: 'No malicious transceiver firmware has been publicly documented.' Also: 'The absence of a public example isn't disproof' and 'Sabotage is possible'.

title: Morgan Stanley: US transceiver curbs may start with 3.2T generation
notes: Reports Morgan Stanley's note that restrictions may start with 3.2T modules ramping around 2028–29.

title: FCC Adds Foreign-Produced Power Inverters to the Covered List
notes: Added 28 Jul 2026 (DA 26-786); previously authorised models can continue to be imported and sold; firmware-update waiver through at least 1 Jan 2029. Update banner 20 Aug 2026.

title: FCC Updates Its Covered List Designation for Foreign-Produced Power Inverters
notes: 20 Aug notice limits coverage to foreign-produced, utility-interactive inverters meeting UL 1741 with remote communications. 'Ordinary data-center power equipment is less likely to be covered' (rectifiers, UPS), though utility-connected remote-capable equipment may need device-specific review.

title: FCC Adds Foreign-Produced Advanced Robotic Devices and Power Inverters to Covered List, Opens Conditional Approval Process
notes: Conditional Approval applications (DoW or DHS for inverters) due by 1 Jan 2028.

title: Fact sheet: FCC updates Covered List to include foreign-made consumer routers, prohibiting approval of new models
notes: 'all consumer-grade routers produced in foreign countries'; does not prohibit existing authorised models.

title: PSHSB announces Conditional Approval and exemption of certain UAS and routers from the Covered List (DA 26-548)
publisher: FCC Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau
notes: Router approvals listed as of 4 Jun 2026 end between 1 Oct and 5 Dec 2027 (1 Oct, 31 Oct, 22 Nov, 5 Dec).

title: FCC Adds Foreign-Produced Consumer Routers to Banned Equipment List
notes: Scope limited to 'consumer-grade networking devices … primarily intended for residential use'; 'would appear to exclude enterprise and industrial-grade networking devices'. OET firmware-update waiver to 1 Mar 2027.

title: InnoLight responds to 1260H designation (exchange announcement)
notes: Company statement (translated): the designation 'does not accord with objective facts'; InnoLight is 'neither a Chinese military company nor a military-civil fusion enterprise'; no material impact on operations.

title: Eoptolink on reported US transceiver curbs
notes: Company said it had noted the news, would watch the impact closely, and that the report had no authoritative source yet.
